boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten named, under-21-safe places in Amherst for viewing art, taking a walk, or gathering outdoors without an admission purchase.

cards.title: Browse the University Museum of Contemporary Art
cards.subtitle: Randolph W. Bromery Center for the Performing Arts, UMass Amherst
cards.notes: Plan a slow loop through the rotating galleries, then use the nearby Fine Arts Center lawn as a place to compare what caught your attention.
cards.short_summary: A campus teaching museum with contemporary exhibitions and always-free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Amherst states that admission to the University Museum of Contemporary Art is always free.
cards.source_title: The University Museum of Contemporary Art: Celebrating 50 Years of Art on Campus
cards.access_notes: The museum is closed for summer; regular hours resume in September. Check the museum page before traveling.

cards.title: See what’s on at Augusta Savage Gallery
cards.subtitle: 180 Infirmary Way, UMass Amherst
cards.notes: Drop in during an exhibition and take time with the wall text; gallery visits work well as a low-key indoor meet-up between classes.
cards.short_summary: A UMass gallery where admission is always free.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Amherst states that admission to the Augusta Savage Gallery is always free.
cards.source_title: Augusta Savage Gallery Announces Spring Exhibition and Events
cards.access_notes: Exhibitions change; confirm the current show and gallery hours before visiting.

cards.title: Visit Herter Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Herter Hall, UMass Amherst
cards.notes: Check the exhibition calendar, then make a short gallery stop part of a walk through the academic core with a friend or visiting family.
cards.short_summary: A long-running campus gallery with free public exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Amherst says Herter Art Gallery exhibitions and receptions are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Herter Art Gallery BFA Thesis Exhibition press release
cards.access_notes: Use the gallery’s current calendar for exhibition dates and opening hours.

cards.title: Take in a Hampden Gallery exhibition
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Center, UMass Amherst
cards.notes: Use the gallery as a focused fifteen-minute pause: choose one work each to revisit, then trade observations outside the Fine Arts Center.
cards.short_summary: A Fine Arts Center gallery with free public exhibitions and events.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Amherst states that all Fine Arts Center gallery events and exhibitions, including Hampden Gallery programming, are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Fine Arts Center Announces Spring 2025 Gallery Exhibitions
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current exhibition and hours with the Fine Arts Center before visiting.

cards.title: Wander the Mead Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Amherst College, 41 Quadrangle Drive
cards.notes: Walk through the collection at your own pace and pick a single object to sketch or describe together; bring only a notebook if you want one.
cards.short_summary: An Amherst College art museum with free public admission.
cards.evidence_claim: Massachusetts’ official tourism site states that the Mead Art Museum offers free public admission six days a week.
cards.access_notes: Check the museum directly for current open days, exhibitions, and any holiday closures.

cards.title: Walk the Puffer’s Pond shoreline
cards.subtitle: Mill River conservation corridor, North Amherst
cards.notes: Follow the established paths for birding, nature walking, or a picnic; keep to marked routes and check town water-quality notices before any swimming.
cards.short_summary: A town conservation-area pond with trails and several passive outdoor uses.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town describes Puffer’s Pond as part of town-owned conservation land open to the public and used free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Swimming conditions can change; consult the Town’s current water-quality information before entering the water.

cards.title: Take a trail walk at Amethyst Brook
cards.subtitle: 132 Pelham Road, Amherst
cards.notes: Choose an established trail for an unhurried walk, and bring water plus insect protection; leave plants, animals, and stream edges undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A named Amherst conservation area maintained within the Town’s trail system.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town identifies Amethyst Brook among conservation areas it manages; Town conservation areas are open free of charge year-round.
cards.access_notes: Trails are for passive recreation; check conditions after storms and respect posted closures.

cards.title: Head out to Mount Pollux
cards.subtitle: Amherst conservation land
cards.notes: Make this an outdoor conversation walk: use maintained paths, pack out everything you bring, and turn back if weather or trail conditions deteriorate.
cards.short_summary: A named town-managed conservation destination for a no-cost walk.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town identifies Mount Pollux among conservation areas it manages; Town conservation areas are open free of charge year-round.
cards.access_notes: Use designated access points and follow any posted conservation-area guidance.

cards.title: Walk the Wentworth Farm trails
cards.subtitle: Amherst conservation land
cards.notes: Use the maintained routes for a daylight walk with friends, keeping gates, habitat areas, and neighboring working-land boundaries exactly as posted.
cards.short_summary: A town-managed conservation area with miles of trails in and around it.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town identifies Wentworth Farm among conservation areas it manages; Town conservation areas are open free of charge year-round.
cards.access_notes: Visit during daylight and respect posted trail, habitat, and private-property boundaries.

cards.title: Cool off at Groff Park Spray Pad
cards.subtitle: 72 Mill Lane, Amherst
cards.notes: Bring a towel and use the spray pad for a warm-weather reset; pair it with the park’s seating, playground, or a walk on the Emily Dickinson Trail.
cards.short_summary: A municipal spray pad with free daily seasonal access.
cards.evidence_claim: The Town of Amherst states that Groff Park Spray Pad is free and open daily.
cards.access_notes: Town guidance lists daily hours of 10 a.m.–8 p.m., with Tuesday opening at noon for maintenance; verify seasonal status before going.
